{"id":"mimid-1wgh.93","title":"Agent JMAP front end: Consent methods, so a stock JMAP client can allow and deny","description":"Found 2026-11-22 while answering what mimid's JMAP push carries.

THE ASYMMETRY. mimid-server's provider endpoint has the full set: Consent/get, Consent/changes, Consent/query and Consent/set (crates/mimid-server/src/jmap/methods/consent.rs), and the EventSource pushes the Consent type (bead mimid-1wgh.12.43). But mimid-agent-jmap, the agent's LOCAL endpoint that users' own clients talk to (decision mimid-1wgh.38: any standard JMAP Chat client talks plaintext JMAP Chat to the local agent), has no Consent method at all: grep finds the word nowhere in the crate.

So the consent decision a user must make to accept an invite from someone new is reachable from IRC (/msg mimid allow <nick>) but not from a JMAP Chat client, which is the default front end. mimid-agent/src/lib.rs:129 records this as a limitation; it is accurate but easy to misread as applying to the provider endpoint too.

WORK. Add Consent to mimid-agent-jmap over the store's own allow/deny, matching what the provider endpoint exposes as closely as the agent's records allow, and push the Consent type on the agent's own EventSource so a client sees a decision made from another front end. Update the lib.rs limitation when it no longer holds.

Why it matters beyond parity: with invites = from-allowed (the default), a user whose only client is a JMAP one cannot act on a pending invite from an unknown sender at all.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-22T21:31:36.879478816Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-22T21:31:36.879478816Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.93","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-22T21:31:36.916892371Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}
